question: Should OpenClaw adopt this core, operator-facing reversible suspension protocol as the long-term host snapshot contract despite its intentionally bounded coverage of only tracked core work?
rationale: Code review can evaluate state-machine correctness, but only maintainers can approve a new public lifecycle API, fixed lease policy, and the core-versus-plugin ownership boundary for external host controllers.

options.title: Adopt the core contract
options.body: Keep the host-neutral RPC and global tracked-work fence, contingent on rebase, exact-head proof, and owner approval of its documented limitations.

options.title: Expose narrower plugin seams
options.body: Add only missing public activity/admission events or helpers and keep snapshot orchestration in a plugin or external controller.

options.title: Defer host suspension
options.body: Pause this PR until the linked lifecycle issue and durable queue work define one consolidated product contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt the core contract
recommendation.body: Keep the host-neutral RPC and global tracked-work fence, contingent on rebase, exact-head proof, and owner approval of its documented limitations.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent merged history across the exact Gateway method, HTTP, protocol, and plugin-runtime surfaces and is already directly engaged with this implementation.
